title: Service Credits for Missed Standing Deliveries on the Office Pantry & Beverage Program
content:
Where a standing delivery was missed, or arrived so short that the pantry stood empty, the client is credited against the invoice for that period. The terms below govern credits on an Office Pantry & Beverage Program programme.

## What a claim must satisfy on time

A credit is allowed only when the claim reaches Larkspur Table no later than the claim window for the pantry tier, counted in calendar days from the day the invoice covering the missed delivery was posted. Claim window days are counted as calendar days from the day after the invoice posting day, every day of the week counts, and a claim arriving on the boundary day itself is still in time; calendar days are never converted into full 24-hour periods.

The day the clock starts from is the posting day recorded against the invoice that covers the missed delivery, identified by its invoice reference on the programme's own records. The test is that the claim arrives not later than the last day of the window.

Boundary reading: on a tier whose claim window runs to 14 calendar days, the day after the invoice posting day is day one, the fourteenth such day is the last day on which a claim is still in time, and a claim reaching the desk on the fifteenth day is out of time. The invoice posting day itself is not counted.

## What the credit comes to

Each missed delivery earns the percentage of the monthly programme fee printed against the tier, and the credits allowed in one billing period are held to the ceiling printed against the same tier.

1. The credit that would be due for the period is that percentage of the monthly programme fee printed against the tier, multiplied by the number of missed standing deliveries counted for the period, rounded to two decimal places.
2. The billing period ceiling is the monthly programme fee printed against the tier taken at the period ceiling percentage printed against the same tier, rounded to two decimal places.
3. The credit allowed is the lower of those two amounts. Where the credits that would be due exceed the billing period ceiling, the ceiling is allowed and the balance of the claim is closed rather than carried forward.

Worked on hypothetical figures: a hypothetical monthly programme fee of 1000.00, a hypothetical per-delivery credit of 10.00 percent and a hypothetical period ceiling of 30.00 percent. Two missed standing deliveries give 200.00 against a ceiling of 300.00, and 200.00 is allowed. Four missed standing deliveries would give 400.00, the ceiling holds the credit at 300.00, and the balance of the claim is closed.

## How a missed delivery is established

Whether a delivery was missed is settled from the delivery records on the programme for that period, and not from the client's recollection of which mornings the shelves were bare. The count is the number of scheduled standing deliveries in the billing period named on the invoice the claim concerns for which no delivery stands recorded.

A delivery missed because the client's building was shut, the loading bay was blocked or access was refused is not a missed delivery for this purpose and earns no credit.
